title: Career Roadmap: Research Engineer
summary: A Research Engineer develops, implements, tests, and improves technical methods to solve complex problems. In data science and artificial intelligence, research engineers turn ideas, mathematical methods, and research papers into working algorithms, experiments, prototypes, and scalable systems.

facts.Current degree: BS in Data Science & Artificial Intelligence

blocks.text: A Research Engineer develops, implements, tests, and improves technical methods to solve complex problems. In data science and artificial intelligence, research engineers turn ideas, mathematical methods, and research papers into working algorithms, experiments, prototypes, and scalable systems.
They often work with research scientists, AI engineers, data scientists, software developers, and domain experts.

The following is a suggested progression. Align it with the official degree syllabus and actual programme duration.
Stage 1 — Programming and mathematical foundations

blocks.label: Suggested period
blocks.text: First year
Learn

items.text: Python programming, functions, object-oriented programming and debugging.
Data structures and algorithms.

blocks.label: Linear algebra
blocks.text: vectors, matrices, eigenvalues and matrix operations.

items.text: Differential calculus, probability and statistics.
Discrete mathematics and basic optimisation.
NumPy, pandas, Matplotlib and Jupyter.
Git, GitHub, Linux and command-line fundamentals.

blocks.text: Practical activities

items.text: Analyse a public dataset and explain the findings.
Implement common algorithms and mathematical operations.
Write clean, reusable Python modules.
Learn to document code and reproduce results.

blocks.label: Milestone
blocks.text: Build a strong programming and mathematical foundation for machine learning.
Stage 2 — Data science and machine learning

blocks.label: Suggested period
blocks.text: Second year
Learn

items.text: Data cleaning, exploratory data analysis and feature engineering.
Regression, classification, clustering and dimensionality reduction.
Model evaluation, cross-validation and error analysis.
Statistical inference, hypothesis testing and confidence intervals.
Scikit-learn and basic model deployment.
SQL, data pipelines and experiment tracking.

blocks.label: Research methodology
blocks.text: defining a problem, reviewing literature and forming hypotheses.
Practical activities

items.text: Compare multiple algorithms on the same dataset.
Investigate data leakage, bias and overfitting.
Reproduce a small machine-learning experiment from a published paper.
Maintain experiment records and report limitations.

blocks.label: Milestone
blocks.text: Design and evaluate machine-learning experiments using sound statistical methods.
Stage 3 — Deep learning and research engineering

blocks.label: Suggested period
blocks.text: Third year
Learn

items.text: Neural networks, backpropagation and optimisation.
CNNs, transformers and sequence models.
PyTorch or TensorFlow; prioritise one framework initially.
GPU computing fundamentals, batching and memory management.
Experimental design, ablation studies and reproducibility.
Docker, testing, logging and experiment tracking.
Reading technical papers and understanding baselines, datasets and evaluation metrics.

blocks.text: Practical activities

items.text: Implement a model from a research paper.
Compare a proposed method with a meaningful baseline.
Test the effect of hyperparameters and architectural choices.
Package the experiment so another person can reproduce it.

blocks.label: Milestone
blocks.text: Convert a research idea into a tested, reproducible implementation.
Stage 4 — Specialisation and career preparation

blocks.label: Suggested period
blocks.text: Final learning phase
Learn

items.text: Choose a research domain and study its key literature.
Advanced optimisation, uncertainty estimation and evaluation.
Distributed training or efficient inference where relevant.
Model interpretability, fairness, robustness and responsible AI.
Research writing, citations and presentation of technical results.
Software engineering practices for maintainable research code.

blocks.text: Practical activities

items.text: Complete a substantial capstone project.
Submit a poster, technical report or research manuscript where appropriate.
Seek a research internship with a university laboratory, R&D group or AI company.
Prepare a technical portfolio and practise research-oriented interviews.

blocks.text: Learn the underlying concepts before adding more tools. A smaller, well-understood toolset is more useful than a large list of unfinished tutorials.
Aim to produce projects that demonstrate research reasoning, not just model training.

blocks.label: Project 1
blocks.text: Comparative machine-learning study

blocks.label: Level
blocks.text: Beginner to intermediate

blocks.label: Build
blocks.text: Select a public classification or regression dataset and compare several suitable algorithms.
Research questions

items.text: Which model performs best under a consistent evaluation protocol?
How do preprocessing and feature selection affect results?
What errors do the models make?

blocks.label: Deliverables
blocks.text: Reproducible notebook, baseline comparison, evaluation metrics, error analysis and technical report.

blocks.label: Project 2
blocks.text: Reproduction of a published deep-learning method

blocks.label: Level
blocks.text: Intermediate

blocks.label: Build
blocks.text: Reimplement a manageable method from a published paper using a publicly available dataset.
Research questions

items.text: Can the reported method be reproduced under documented conditions?
How sensitive are results to random seeds, data preprocessing and hyperparameters?
Which results are consistent with the paper, and which differ?

blocks.label: Deliverables
blocks.text: Paper summary, implementation, baseline, experiment logs, comparison table and limitations.

blocks.label: Project 3
blocks.text: Research-paper question-answering system

blocks.label: Level
blocks.text: Intermediate to advanced

blocks.label: Build
blocks.text: Create a retrieval-augmented question-answering system over a curated collection of research papers.
Research questions

items.text: Does retrieval improve answer quality compared with a baseline?
How do chunking and retrieval settings affect evidence selection?
Does the system correctly identify when the papers do not contain an answer?

blocks.label: Deliverables
blocks.text: Search pipeline, source-linked answers, evaluation dataset, retrieval metrics and error analysis.

blocks.label: Project 4
blocks.text: Model efficiency and performance benchmark

blocks.label: Level
blocks.text: Advanced

blocks.label: Build
blocks.text: Compare two or more models or inference configurations under consistent conditions.
Research questions

items.text: What is the trade-off between quality, latency and memory?
How do batch size, quantisation or model size affect performance?
Can efficiency be improved without unacceptable quality loss?

blocks.label: Deliverables
blocks.text: Benchmarking scripts, documented hardware, repeated measurements, plots and recommendations.

For every project, include a clear problem statement, related-work summary, dataset source, experimental setup, baselines, metrics, results, limitations and reproducibility instructions. Do not claim that a project is novel research unless you have investigated related work sufficiently.
Look for opportunities in university research groups, AI laboratories, corporate R&D teams and research-oriented startups.

blocks.text: Application preparation

items.text: Build two substantial projects with reproducible results.
Read papers relevant to the research group you are applying to.
Prepare a concise technical résumé highlighting programming, mathematics and experimentation.
Maintain a clean GitHub portfolio with instructions to reproduce your work.
Contact research supervisors with a specific explanation of how your skills match their work.
Practise coding, probability, linear algebra, machine learning and project discussions.

blocks.text: A research internship may be competitive. Strong coursework, thoughtful experiments, good documentation and relevant recommendations can strengthen an application.

blocks.text: Job titles vary between employers. Some research engineering positions require graduate study, publications or previous research experience, while others focus on strong engineering implementation skills.
Possible next steps include:

items.text: Master's in Computer Science, Artificial Intelligence or Data Science.
Master's in Machine Learning, Robotics or Computer Vision.
Specialised postgraduate study in computational science or scientific computing.
Research-based master's or PhD for more theoretical or academic research roles.

blocks.text: For each programme, verify accepted bachelor's qualifications, prerequisite mathematics and computing courses, entrance examinations and funding requirements. A BS qualification does not automatically guarantee eligibility for every postgraduate programme.
Stage 1 — Research Intern or Junior Engineer
Implement established methods, run experiments and document results.
Stage 2 — Research Engineer
Own experiments, develop research software and evaluate alternative approaches.
Stage 3 — Senior or Specialist Research Engineer
Lead complex implementations, improve research infrastructure and guide experimental design.
Stage 4 — Research Lead, R&D Lead or Research Scientist pathway
Direct research programmes or move toward scientific leadership, depending on qualifications and demonstrated research contributions.

Research Engineer and Research Scientist are not interchangeable titles in every organisation. Research engineering often emphasises implementation, experimentation and systems; scientist roles may place greater emphasis on developing new methods and research directions.

A job-ready graduate should be able to:

items.text: Translate a technical question into a testable research problem.
Read and critically assess relevant research papers.
Implement algorithms and machine-learning models.
Design experiments with appropriate baselines and evaluation metrics.
Analyse failures, explain limitations and interpret results.
Write maintainable, reproducible research code.
Communicate findings through reports, presentations and demonstrations.
Collaborate with engineers, researchers and domain specialists.

blocks.label: Recommended priority
blocks.text: Master Python and mathematics first, then machine learning and deep learning. Learn to reproduce existing research before attempting to develop a new method. A portfolio showing sound experiments, reliable code and honest interpretation of results will be more persuasive than a collection of projects that only demonstrate model training.
